explanation: The MCP layer for rustre-loader-macho only exposes the high-level `macho_info` tool, which requires a full Mach-O binary path and returns aggregated parser results. The Python validator only re-implements low-level deterministic helpers (LEB128, adler32, Shannon entropy, little/big-endian reads, C-string reads, FAT magic detection, FAT arch list, function-starts delta decoding, Swift relative-pointer resolution, vm->fileoff resolution, swift mangling prefix tests, notarization magic scan, lossless integer casts). None of these helpers are individually exposed via MCP wire tools. A direct per-function MCP-vs-validator comparison is therefore not possible without authoring a dedicated Rust test harness binary that exports these helpers over stdio.
notes: No mismatch detected because there is no shared surface to compare. Crate source under crates/rustre-loader-macho/src was not modified. To enable real validation, expose helpers (read_uleb128, adler32, byte_entropy, detect_fat, list_arches, function_starts_parse, resolve_relative_ptr, casts::*) as MCP tools, or build a thin Rust CLI harness that mirrors the validator's DISPATCH map.
